subject: Trying to reduce duplication in the code when using ddply

messages.author: 0600694caf57b8fb
messages.subject: Trying to reduce duplication in the code when using ddply
parts:
Hello,

I am using ddply from package 'plyr' to generate different layers that
later I plot using ggplot2:

layer1<-ddply(data,.(var1,var2,var3),function1)
layer2<-ddply(data,.(var1,var2,var3),function2)
...

The issue I have is that sometimes I want to reduce the grouping
variables let's say from var1, var2 and var3 to var1 and var2 and then
i need to change the code of each 'layer' by hand to:

layer1<-ddply(data,.(var1,var2),function1)
layer2<-ddply(data,.(var1,var2),function2)
...

Does someone know any trick i can use to define a string of grouping
variables so that i can use:

layer1<-ddply(data,.(groupingVariables),function1)
layer2<-ddply(data,.(groupingVariables),function2)
...


thanks

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Trying to reduce duplication in the code when using ddply
parts:
Hi Dani,

You can just pass in a vector of variable names: c("var1", "var2")

Hadley
